nodes.label: tiktok.html recipe fixture

nodes.rationale: Holds the DM count in a <sup> (3 in the fixture). The sibling inbox-icon carries 9, so a fixture that matched the wrong hook would silently report 9 — which is what makes this fixture a real oracle rather than a smoke test.

nodes.label: data-e2e="dm-new-chatbox" ready + css gate

nodes.label: data-e2e="dm-new-conversation-item" / "-nickname" rows

nodes.label: DivDrawerContainer hosts the DM conversation list

nodes.label: Appearance Settings Panel

nodes.label: Menu Position Setting

nodes.label: Theme Setting

nodes.label: Light/Dark Theme Parity

nodes.label: Waking Interstitial

nodes.label: Goetia engineering guardrails
nodes.rationale: Invariants distilled from the 2026-08-07 review and security audit; breaking one is a regression even if tests pass.

nodes.label: Definition of done
nodes.rationale: lint + typecheck + test green, e2e for main/preload/renderer wiring, and a real package:mac build that launches for packaging changes.

nodes.label: Chat ONLY product principle
nodes.rationale: Goetia shows each service's chat surface and nothing else — no feeds, shops or menus (user decision 2026-08-07); every containment mechanism below exists to keep that true.

nodes.label: Recipe CSS hides host chrome
nodes.rationale: Chrome hiding is gated on the chat surface being mounted so login and captcha pages stay untouched (the shopee lesson), and uses display:none so textContent stays readable for count().

nodes.label: hideChrome per-tick hook
nodes.rationale: Chrome with no stable selector (hash-classed rails, role=button icons) can only be hidden per tick from JS; it must never return the chat surface or an ancestor of it, and it is cosmetic — chatPaths remains the containment.

nodes.label: chatPaths snapback containment
nodes.rationale: Sites that are more than chat declare chatPaths: once a document has been on a chat path, SPA routing off all of them navigates back to the service URL, floored by SNAPBACK_MIN_INTERVAL_MS; login flows never snap because they never reach a chat path.

nodes.label: Reload returns the view to the chat URL
nodes.rationale: User-initiated reload is the way back when a site's own links wander off chat, so it goes through views.refresh; crash auto-reload keeps the current URL instead.
nodes.norm_label: reload returns the view to the chat url

nodes.label: Enable/disable lives on Home, never Settings
nodes.rationale: Composition behind a modal is what let a service view bury the modal it was toggled from, so Settings never gets an enable toggle back.
nodes.norm_label: enable/disable lives on home, never settings

nodes.label: Zero enabled services means zero service views
nodes.rationale: Fresh installs start fully disabled and the welcome screen is derived from settings rather than a flag, so no view may exist while everything is disabled.
nodes.norm_label: zero enabled services means zero service views

nodes.label: Launch restores the surface you left
nodes.rationale: resolveStartupSurface reopens the last active service or Home; a recorded service that is now disabled or gone opens Home rather than silently substituting another.
nodes.norm_label: launch restores the surface you left

nodes.label: One sound per message
nodes.rationale: Most services ding in-page themselves, so Goetia sounds only banners the page could not have made (synthetic ones); soundOptions is the single decision point, and setting sound without silent is a bug because macOS reads the name while Windows/Linux read the flag.

nodes.label: Mute means silence, never blindness
nodes.rationale: Muting suppresses the banner and the page's own audio but leaves badges alone; aggregateBadges must stay ignorant of mute because the badge is how a muted service is still found.

nodes.label: Global mute goes through ctx.setGlobalMuted
nodes.rationale: One path persists, re-mutes the views and rebuilds both menus, whose checkmarks are baked in at build time; calling settings.update({globalMuted}) directly desynchronizes them.

nodes.label: Accelerator declared in the app menu only
nodes.rationale: The tray's copy of the mute item must carry no accelerator, or one keypress fires the toggle twice.
nodes.norm_label: accelerator declared in the app menu only

nodes.label: Shell sandboxed, service views unisolated
nodes.rationale: The shell window keeps contextIsolation and sandbox on; service views need them off for the recipe workarounds, so hardening happens around that boundary and nodeIntegration is never added.

nodes.label: src/shared stays process-agnostic
nodes.rationale: No electron and no DOM imports, so shared code is safe to bundle into both main and the sandboxed preload.

nodes.label: Pure decision logic in lib/, thin wiring elsewhere
nodes.rationale: Decisions live in unit-tested lib/ helpers so views.ts, index.ts and ipc-handlers.ts stay wiring that cannot hide logic from tests.
nodes.norm_label: pure decision logic in lib/, thin wiring elsewhere

nodes.label: No visible view while an overlay is open
nodes.rationale: Service views are layered above the shell renderer, so a visible view covers settings, quick switcher or Home; activation resolves with show:false and showActive() presents it when the surface closes — startup included.
nodes.norm_label: no visible view while an overlay is open

nodes.label: Electron fuses invariant
nodes.rationale: runAsNode, NODE_OPTIONS and CLI inspect stay off while cookie encryption, asar integrity and onlyLoadAppFromAsar stay on; keys are schema-checked, and enableRunAsNode is not one — a bad key fails the whole config.

nodes.label: Minimal macOS entitlements
nodes.rationale: Only allow-jit, allow-unsigned-executable-memory and disable-library-validation; allow-dyld-environment-variables would reopen the injection path the fuses close.

nodes.label: Every IPC channel is classified and sender-checked
nodes.rationale: Channels register through the wrapper that enforces ipcSenderAllowed: shell-only channels are listed in SHELL_ONLY_CHANNELS, service channels carry a serviceId validated against the sending frame, so no attacker-controllable payload can persist settings, spawn or navigate.
nodes.norm_label: every ipc channel is classified and sender-checked

nodes.label: External links only via isSafeExternalUrl
nodes.rationale: shell.openExternal is reachable only for web schemes, so a hostile page cannot hand file:, smb: or custom schemes to the OS.

nodes.label: Permissions granted only via permissionAllowed
nodes.rationale: Origin-checked grants limited to notifications and media; broadening the allowlist or dropping the origin check hands a redirected page the service's privileges.

nodes.label: Navigation containment not yet wired
nodes.rationale: isNavigationAllowed/ALLOWED_HOSTS exist but the will-navigate guard is deliberately not attached until every service's real auth-redirect hosts are confirmed by a live login pass.

nodes.label: One throttled notification path
nodes.rationale: All banners flow through NotificationRouter with a per-service rate limit; a second path would be unthrottled and let a page spam the OS.

nodes.label: Renderer CSP lockdown
nodes.rationale: index.html and loading.html keep default-src 'self' plus object-src none, base-uri self and frame-src none; no remote assets and no innerHTML in the shell.

nodes.label: count() cost rules
nodes.rationale: Recipe polling runs at full interval even while hidden (websockets exempt the page from Chromium throttling), so count() must be cheap and must always settle: no computed-style or bounding-rect sweeps over large lists, no whole-store IndexedDB reads, and never a promise that cannot resolve — COUNT_TIMEOUT_MS is a backstop, not a licence.

nodes.label: Report on change only
nodes.rationale: The runner de-dups counts and reports stale only on the transition into stale, and MainState.setRuntime skips the broadcast on a no-op patch; per-tick broadcasts must not return.

nodes.label: Tile reorder is drag-local
nodes.rationale: Reorder.Group fires onReorder on every crossing, so a renderer draft order sends service:reorder once on drag end; wiring onReorder straight to IPC would mean one settings write, broadcast and menu rebuild per crossing. The draft clears when the broadcast lands so the drop never snaps back.

nodes.label: Bounded timers and listeners
nodes.rationale: Every interval, timeout and webContents/session listener is cleared on destroy and on quit, deferred callbacks are guarded by !isDestroyed(), and polls are capped (startReadyPoll at READY_POLL_MAX_ATTEMPTS).

nodes.label: Crash count forgotten only after a dwell
nodes.rationale: ResilienceManager forgets a service's crash count only after DWELL_MS of uptime; resetting it on every did-finish-load defeats the auto-reload cap.
nodes.norm_label: crash count forgotten only after a dwell

nodes.label: Coalesced window resize layout
nodes.rationale: Resize goes through scheduleLayout() so a burst costs one layout pass; per-event heavy work in the resize handler is banned.

nodes.label: One long-lived window
nodes.rationale: With close-to-tray off the window is destroyed and the app quits, so broadcast() and tray handlers stay guarded by win.isDestroyed().

nodes.label: Adding a service checklist
nodes.rationale: Registration, recipe, fixture-as-oracle, ALLOWED_HOSTS entry and notification icons must all land together; no extra permissions and no new unvalidated IPC channel.

nodes.label: Packaging and fuse verification
nodes.rationale: Fuses are read back from the packaged app via @electron/fuses getCurrentFuseWire because the CLI is not on PATH; 'damaged' means a broken signature (a different bug) while the malware-verification dialog means only a missing notarization ticket.

nodes.label: Ad-hoc signature re-prompts for Safe Storage
nodes.rationale: Each build's designated requirement is its own cdhash, so every rebuild looks like a new app to the keychain item enableCookieEncryption creates — expected, answer Always Allow, never turn the fuse off to silence it.
nodes.norm_label: ad-hoc signature re-prompts for safe storage

nodes.label: Goetia (multi-service chat client)
nodes.rationale: Nine chat services in one Electron window — WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Zalo, TikTok, Shopee — each a self-contained recipe so the roster grows without the rest noticing.

nodes.label: Chat only, unlike other multi-service clients
nodes.rationale: Every other client embeds the whole site, feed and all; Goetia hides host chrome and pins more-than-chat services to their chat paths so routing away snaps back.
nodes.norm_label: chat only, unlike other multi-service clients

nodes.label: Local only, isolated persist sessions
nodes.rationale: No server, account or telemetry; each service gets its own persist:<id> session so no two logins ever see each other.

nodes.label: Badges that don't lie
nodes.rationale: One unread recipe per service locked to a DOM fixture in the test suite; when a service redesigns, the tile shows a grey stale dot instead of a confident zero.

nodes.label: Native notifications with per-service icons
nodes.rationale: Per-service and global mute, a per-service rate limit so a page cannot spam, plus synthetic notifications for services that never fire one in-page.

nodes.label: Hardening summary
nodes.rationale: Fuses, a sandboxed shell, an IPC sender policy stopping one service frame impersonating another, origin-checked permissions, a locked-down renderer CSP and a build-provenance attestation on every installer.

nodes.label: Home: summon, banish, dispel
nodes.rationale: A pick only changes sides once confirmed — the button spells out the change and Dispel throws the edit away — while dragging a summoned tile takes effect on its own, so reordering never rides along with an enable.

nodes.label: How an unread count reaches you
nodes.rationale: page DOM/IndexedDB -> recipe count() -> ~2s de-duped runner -> unread:update -> MainState -> rail badge, dock/taskbar and tray tooltip; a throwing count() lands as a grey stale dot. Counts report only on change so a hidden service costs almost nothing.
nodes.norm_label: how an unread count reaches you

nodes.label: Install: getting past the first-launch warning
nodes.rationale: macOS 15+ says 'Apple could not verify … free of malware' with Move to Trash highlighted; the two working escapes are Privacy & Security -> Open Anyway or xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine, and Windows needs More info -> Run anyway.
nodes.norm_label: install: getting past the first-launch warning

nodes.label: Checking the download is genuine
nodes.rationale: Both bypasses amount to telling the OS to trust the file, so every release ships SHA256SUMS.txt plus a GitHub build-provenance attestation tying each installer to the commit and workflow run that built it.

nodes.label: Keyboard shortcuts and rail interactions
nodes.rationale: Cmd/Ctrl+1…9 jump, +K quick switcher, +0 Home, +R or F5 reload, +Shift+M mute all, right-click a tile to mute, drag to reorder.

nodes.label: Goetia Safe Storage keychain prompt (user-facing)
nodes.rationale: Saved logins are locked with a key in the login keychain; because the app is unsigned macOS treats each version as a different app, so it asks again after every update — Deny leaves the sessions locked.

nodes.label: Self-checking updates
nodes.rationale: A few-second notice plus a dot on the settings icon open the download page; Goetia cannot install its own update because it is not code-signed.

nodes.label: Muting means silence, not blindness (user-facing)
nodes.rationale: A muted service raises no banner and its page audio is silenced too, including calls and voice notes, but its unread badge keeps counting.

nodes.label: corepack pnpm invocation
nodes.rationale: pnpm may not be on PATH with Homebrew Node, so commands run through corepack against the version pinned in packageManager; tools that spawn pnpm themselves (electron-builder) need the corepack shims on PATH.

nodes.label: Reproducing the Gatekeeper prompt by hand
nodes.rationale: A locally built app is not quarantined and opens with no warning, so seeing what a downloader sees requires writing com.apple.quarantine by hand and expecting spctl to reject it.
nodes.norm_label: reproducing the gatekeeper prompt by hand

nodes.label: Releases cut by pushing a version tag
nodes.rationale: The tag must match package.json's version.
nodes.norm_label: releases cut by pushing a version tag

nodes.label: Recipes adapted from ferdium-recipes
nodes.rationale: Apache-2.0 upstream; when a service redesigns, the selector and its fixture are fixed together because pnpm test locks them to each other.

nodes.label: Ember Portal branding
nodes.rationale: A summoning circle as pure energy matching the ember accent (dark #FF9E2C, light #E8590C); SVG sources live in resources/ and PNGs are regenerated with rsvg-convert.

nodes.label: Viber intentionally absent
nodes.rationale: It has no web client to embed.

nodes.label: pnpm media screenshot regeneration
nodes.rationale: Relaunches the app against a throwaway profile and rewrites docs/media/*.png, so the repo never contains a signed-in capture.

nodes.label: Harmless task_policy_set startup error
nodes.rationale: Chromium failing to put a child process under macOS App Nap — not ours, and nothing breaks.

nodes.label: Goetia features and verification inventory
nodes.rationale: Doubles as a regression checklist: 'Verified' means an automated test asserts it, 'Manual' means no automated coverage exists.

nodes.label: Verification at a glance
nodes.rationale: 147 Vitest unit tests across 32 files, 2 Playwright-Electron specs, clean tsc and Biome; everything else is listed as a manual check.

nodes.label: Unread counts and badge surfaces
nodes.rationale: Rail tile badge, macOS dock badge, Windows taskbar canvas overlay and tray tooltip all derive from aggregateBadges, which knows nothing about mute so a muted service still reaches every surface.

nodes.label: Notification features
nodes.rationale: Native banners with per-service icons, synthetic notifications for pages that never notify, a Notification shim rerouting the page API, per-service and global mute through ctx.setGlobalMuted, sound only for synthetic banners, and a per-service rate limit.

nodes.label: Service lifecycle and resilience features
nodes.rationale: Waking overlay, bounded readiness poll, capped crash auto-reload with a stable-uptime dwell, config-gated hibernation, trusted-click keep-alive for Zalo/Shopee, and Zalo's visibility spoof.

nodes.label: Settings, persistence and update check
nodes.rationale: New services reconcile in disabled without losing prefs, a malformed settings.json is coerced per field instead of bricking startup, and the update check builds its download URL from a validated version rather than the API payload.

nodes.label: Per-service recipe inventory
nodes.rationale: WhatsApp reads model-storage IndexedDB, Messenger scans the DOM and synthesizes, Telegram/Discord read badge counts, Zalo adds keepRendered plus visibility spoof, Shopee reshapes the mini-chat widget.

nodes.label: Not yet wired / known limits
nodes.rationale: The navigation guard is unattached pending live-login verification, distribution is unsigned so downloads are gated, and package:win needs a Windows machine.

nodes.label: Manual checks with no automated coverage
nodes.norm_label: manual checks with no automated coverage

nodes.label: Service switch needed an explicit state.touch()
nodes.rationale: activateService relied on setRuntime({hibernated:false}) to broadcast, but the new no-op guard skips the broadcast when nothing changes and a non-hibernated service is the normal case, so the renderer never learned the new activeId until a reload; activate.ts now calls ctx.state.touch() explicitly.
nodes.norm_label: service switch needed an explicit state.touch()

nodes.label: Goetia v1 implementation plan
nodes.rationale: Fourteen TDD tasks shipping v1 for five services (whatsapp, messenger, telegram, discord, zalo) on macOS + Windows.

nodes.label: Single-window shell with a view per service
nodes.rationale: One BrowserWindow whose base renderer is the shell chrome plus one WebContentsView per service; main is the single source of truth, holding settings and runtime state and broadcasting a ShellState snapshot over typed IPC.
nodes.norm_label: single-window shell with a view per service

nodes.label: ServiceViewManager with isolated sessions
nodes.rationale: Each view gets a persist:<id> partition, an unisolated preload, spellcheck en-US/vi, a window-open handler that denies in-app opens, and load/crash hooks; layout keeps it filling everything right of the rail.

nodes.label: chromeUserAgent strips Electron tokens
nodes.rationale: WhatsApp and Google login flows block unknown UA tokens, so the app presents a plain Chrome UA.

nodes.label: SettingsStore over conf
nodes.rationale: conf (electron-store's engine) is used directly so settings are testable without an Electron runtime; the cwd is userData in production and a tmp dir in tests.

nodes.label: MainState snapshot and broadcast pipeline
nodes.rationale: Every mutation notifies subscribers; snapshot() orders services per settings, resolves per-service runtime defaults and carries the already-resolved effective theme, and plain field writes need an explicit touch().

nodes.label: Typed IPC contract
nodes.rationale: RendererToMain / MainToRenderer channel maps plus R2M_CHANNELS as the preload's send allowlist, so the contextBridge API can only forward known channels.

nodes.label: Recipe framework and runner
nodes.rationale: A per-service Recipe with intervalMs and count(doc), driven by startRecipe which reports only on change and marks counts stale when count() throws; unreadFromTitle is the shared title fallback.

nodes.label: Badge aggregation across dock, overlay and rail
nodes.rationale: aggregateBadges sums unmuted direct counts and flags indirect-only; badgeLabel caps at 9+ because the OS overlay is tiny; Windows renders a canvas PNG data URL sent over badge:overlay.
nodes.norm_label: badge aggregation across dock, overlay and rail

nodes.label: Notification pipeline and shouldNotify
nodes.rationale: The service preload wraps window.Notification and forwards notification:fired; NotificationRouter shows the native banner and a click focuses the window and activates the service, gated by the pure shouldNotify mute rule.

nodes.label: Hibernation controller and rules
nodes.rationale: shouldHibernate never touches the active, already-hibernated or excluded service; a 60s sweep destroys idle views and the normal activate path recreates them.

nodes.label: Tray, close-to-tray and autostart
nodes.rationale: A template tray icon gives macOS automatic light/dark; the tray menu mirrors show/hide and mute-all, and launchAtLogin maps to app.setLoginItemSettings.

nodes.label: Quick switcher, fuzzyScore and app menu accelerators
nodes.rationale: fuzzyScore matches subsequences and rewards prefixes and streaks; buildAppMenu derives CmdOrCtrl+1..9 from the current order and is rebuilt on reorder.
nodes.norm_label: quick switcher, fuzzyscore and app menu accelerators

nodes.label: Crash resilience with exponential backoff
nodes.rationale: backoffDelay doubles from 1s to a 30s cap and ResilienceManager gives up after five auto-reloads, leaving crashed sticky until a manual retry.

nodes.label: Design tokens and reduced-motion kill switch
nodes.rationale: tokens.css carries the spec palette verbatim per theme plus radius/font scales, and a prefers-reduced-motion block that must stay last so it wins.
nodes.norm_label: design tokens and reduced-motion kill switch

nodes.label: E2E smoke test and packaging targets
nodes.rationale: A --goetia-e2e flag injects a fake unread so Playwright can assert badge propagation without a live login; packaging emits a dmg on macOS and an NSIS installer on Windows.
nodes.norm_label: e2e smoke test and packaging targets

nodes.label: Agents never commit (plan-wide constraint)
nodes.rationale: Every checkpoint stops and asks the repo owner to run /grimoire-core:commit; writing GRIMOIRE_COMMIT_MSG.txt would forge their approval, and this overrides every skill default.

nodes.label: Release workflow implementation plan
nodes.rationale: On a v* tag push, build unsigned mac dmgs (arm64 + x64) and a Windows nsis exe and attach them to a GitHub Release.

nodes.label: Two-phase build matrix and release job
nodes.rationale: A macos/windows matrix uploads run artifacts and a tag-only release job downloads and attaches them; pnpm/action-setup reads the pinned packageManager (more robust on Windows than corepack enable and required before setup-node's pnpm cache), bash defaults make multiline steps fail fast, fail-fast means one bad OS blocks the release, and if-no-files-found: error catches a silent packaging failure.
nodes.norm_label: two-phase build matrix and release job

nodes.label: Arch-suffixed dmg artifact names
nodes.rationale: An explicit artifactName gives the x64 dmg its arch suffix (the default omits it) and the zip target is dropped, so the workflow globs and README names stay predictable.

nodes.label: Tag-matches-package.json guard
nodes.rationale: A tag whose version differs from package.json fails the job before anything is published.

nodes.label: publish: null plus --publish never
nodes.rationale: Belt and braces: publish: null keeps local packaging from publishing, and the CLI flag stops electron-builder auto-publishing on CI tag builds when a token happens to be present.

nodes.label: Notification service icons plan
nodes.rationale: Show a brand-coloured service tile in every OS banner so services are distinguishable without reading the text.

nodes.label: Build-time tile rasteriser
nodes.rationale: A script nests each logo SVG whole inside a 128px rounded tile so its own viewBox scales — no path extraction to re-parse when a logo changes — and @resvg/resvg-js stays a devDependency so nothing new enters the runtime graph; ratios are derived from constants, never hardcoded pixels.

nodes.label: Full-bleed and macOS-inset variants
nodes.rationale: macOS gets a padded tile so it reads smaller than the app icon in the banner slot; every other platform gets the full-bleed one. The opaque brand background is what keeps the tile legible in both Light and Dark.

nodes.label: resolveIcons: paths resolved once at startup
nodes.rationale: A missing asset silently drops out of the map rather than costing a stat call on every notification, and no image is ever decoded into or retained by the app.
nodes.norm_label: resolveicons: paths resolved once at startup

nodes.label: NotificationRouter icon and title wiring
nodes.rationale: The shouldNotify mute gate stays first in handle(), ahead of any icon work; the icon is spread in conditionally so an absent asset is simply omitted.

nodes.label: notificationTitle falls back to the service name
nodes.rationale: The title now carries the sender alone, so a recipe reporting an empty one would otherwise raise a headless banner.
nodes.norm_label: notificationtitle falls back to the service name

nodes.label: Assets shipped outside the asar
nodes.rationale: extraResources drops the icons beside the asar so the path is one the OS can actually open; the packaged run is the only thing that exercises the process.resourcesPath branch.

nodes.label: NativeImage fallback if a path icon is ignored
nodes.rationale: Electron 43 may honour icon only as a NativeImage on darwin; if the path form draws nothing, the commit message must record it so nobody 'simplifies' it back.
nodes.norm_label: nativeimage fallback if a path icon is ignored

nodes.label: Service loading screen (waking overlay) plan
nodes.rationale: Cover every service load — cold start, hibernation wake, reload, crash retry — until the chat UI is usable, with a 10s reveal fallback.

nodes.label: Recipe ready(doc) chat-usable check
nodes.rationale: Messenger is ready once chat rows render; Shopee only once the mini-chat is expanded, i.e. after the keep-alive click landed. ServiceMeta.waitForReady mirrors whether a recipe defines ready(), enforced by a reflection test.

nodes.label: waking runtime flag and loading:state channel
nodes.rationale: ServiceRuntime.waking defaults false and rides the normal ShellState broadcast; a separate main->overlay loading:state channel carries theme and service name to the cover page.
nodes.norm_label: waking runtime flag and loading:state channel

nodes.label: startReadyPoll in the service preload
nodes.rationale: Polls ready() every 250ms, reports service:ready exactly once per document then stops; a throwing ready() counts as not-ready because main's reveal timeout is the backstop, so a page can never stay covered forever.

nodes.label: WakingTracker and endsWake rules
nodes.rationale: load-finished reveals only services without a ready() check; recipe-ready, timeout, crash, load-failure and destruction always reveal, because the cover must never outlive its view or trap a Retry. A reload mid-wake re-arms the 10s timer.

nodes.label: LoadingOverlay WebContentsView
nodes.rationale: An app-owned sandboxed view stacked above the active service, loaded hidden at startup so the first show paints instantly, with a per-theme background so no white flash precedes the page; show() re-adds it at the top of the z-order every call, and it hides while settings or the switcher are open. The service page stays visible and interactive underneath so keep-alive trusted clicks still work.

nodes.label: Ember-portal loading page
nodes.rationale: A second renderer entry reusing the app icon's portal artwork (spinning ring, breathing core) with a 'Waking {Service}…' caption; tokens.css already supplies the theme variables and the reduced-motion kill switch.

nodes.label: Rail tiles breathe while waking
nodes.rationale: The .tile-breathe animation overrides the utility opacity classes while it runs, which is exactly the breathing effect, and doubles as the e2e handle for wake start and reveal.

nodes.label: Shopee chat-focus plan
nodes.rationale: Render the buyer mini-chat full-window with real unread counts and auto-open, with Shopee disabled by default.

nodes.label: Entry URL moves off the anti-bot gate
nodes.rationale: /webchat hits Shopee's anti-bot wall (verify/captcha, scene=crawler_item), so the service lands on the shopping homepage and the recipe reshapes the widget instead.
nodes.norm_label: entry url moves off the anti-bot gate

nodes.label: Structural selectors only, never hashed classes
nodes.rationale: Only #main and #shopee-mini-chat-embedded are stable; everything below them is build-hashed, so the recipe keys on ids and child structure (expanded = wrapper with two children, collapsed = single-child pill).
nodes.norm_label: structural selectors only, never hashed classes

nodes.label: count() reads the widget badge via chatHeader
nodes.rationale: chatHeader returns the header row when expanded and the whole wrapper when collapsed — the one place the unread digits live — and falls back to the page title when the host is absent so blank.html yields zero without throwing.
nodes.norm_label: count() reads the widget badge via chatheader

nodes.label: keepAlive opens the collapsed pill
nodes.rationale: Page-JS synthetic clicks are untrusted, so the runner's trusted-click path (rate-limited to one per 30s) targets the pill; a laid-out-but-tiny rect means the view is not really laid out yet, so no click is issued.

nodes.label: Chat-focus CSS gated on the expanded state
nodes.rationale: Amended during live verification: ungated rules stretched the collapsed pill into a blank view and would have hidden a captcha, so every rule is now gated with :has on the expanded panel and the collapsed page stays untouched for login flows.
nodes.norm_label: chat-focus css gated on the expanded state

nodes.label: Shopee disabled by default
nodes.rationale: DEFAULT_SETTINGS.disabled.shopee flips to true, leaving messenger and zalo as the only enabled services and the e2e rail count at two.

nodes.label: Code signing and notarization (parked)
nodes.rationale: Not started and blocked on paid developer enrollments, so it is a parked decision record rather than an executable plan.

nodes.label: Designated requirement stability explains the keychain prompt
nodes.rationale: A keychain ACL trusts the creating app by its designated requirement; under ad-hoc signing the DR collapses to the binary's cdhash, which changes every rebuild, so macOS sees a different program asking for someone else's item. A Developer ID DR (identifier + anchor apple generic + team OU) is stable across builds and stops the prompt for good.
nodes.norm_label: designated requirement stability explains the keychain prompt

nodes.label: Turning the cookie-encryption fuse off is not an option
nodes.rationale: Chromium would fall back to a hardcoded key, leaving every service's session cookies readable on disk.
nodes.norm_label: turning the cookie-encryption fuse off is not an option

nodes.label: Signing prerequisites and cost
nodes.rationale: Apple Developer Program at USD 99/year yields Developer ID certs and notarization; Windows OV certs cost 200-400/year and still need reputation, EV clears SmartScreen at once. macOS is worth doing first because it is cheaper and fixes the recurring prompt.

nodes.label: Open question: fuse flipping vs signing order
nodes.rationale: resetAdHocDarwinSignature exists because flipping fuses invalidates the signature and macOS refuses Notification Center registration for an unsigned bundle; with a real identity it should become false, but electron-builder's step ordering must be confirmed empirically, and asar integrity validation interacts with any post-signing modification.
nodes.norm_label: open question: fuse flipping vs signing order

nodes.label: One-time migration cost of switching identities
nodes.rationale: The DR changes one final time so the first signed build prompts once more; sessions survive because only the ACL entry grows, not the key.
nodes.norm_label: one-time migration cost of switching identities

nodes.label: Reliability and performance remediation plan
nodes.rationale: Fixes a window-lifecycle crash, a defeated crash-reload cap, unbounded background polling, a broadcast storm, resize thrash, a startup brick and several leaks; decision logic moves into pure helpers so wiring stays thin and the recipe fixtures remain the oracle.

nodes.label: Close-to-tray off must quit, not zombie
nodes.rationale: With close-to-tray off the X button means quit, so the process never lingers with live timers and a tray behind a destroyed window; broadcast() also returns early once the window is destroyed.
nodes.norm_label: close-to-tray off must quit, not zombie

nodes.label: Crash-reload cap survives post-load crashes
nodes.rationale: noteRecovered arms a DWELL_MS timer instead of clearing the count immediately, and a crash inside the dwell cancels it, so a load-crash-reload loop can no longer reset MAX_AUTO_RELOADS every cycle.

nodes.label: Readiness poll attempt cap
nodes.rationale: READY_POLL_MAX_ATTEMPTS gives up once main's 10s reveal has surely fired, because a later ready() cannot re-cover the current load and polling forever on a login wall only burns CPU.

nodes.label: Stale reported once per transition
nodes.rationale: A stale flag in the runner turns a per-tick failure storm into one report, and a successful count re-arms it so a later failure is a new transition.

nodes.label: setRuntime skips the no-op broadcast
nodes.rationale: isNoOp compares the patch field-by-field (unread structurally) so a repeated identical patch no longer touches subscribers and re-broadcasts a snapshot.

nodes.label: Coalesced resize layout
nodes.rationale: A scheduled flag collapses a burst of resize events into one layout pass per ~16ms tick instead of one per event.

nodes.label: Single-pass Messenger unread detection
nodes.rationale: One computed-style read per element replaces two overlapping querySelectorAll sweeps while preserving the fixture count of 3; the blue-dominant test excludes presence-green dots.

nodes.label: Per-field settings.json coercion
nodes.rationale: A non-array order or non-object record is coerced back to defaults instead of throwing, so a hand-mangled file cannot brick startup; normalize is exported under an alias purely so the test can reach it.

nodes.label: connectShell returns its unsubscribe
nodes.rationale: Returning the unsubscribe makes React register it as the effect cleanup automatically, so a shell reload stops stacking shell:state listeners without touching App.tsx.

nodes.label: Deferred trustedClick toggle guarded
nodes.rationale: The 300ms re-hide is tracked per service, checks isDestroyed() before running, and is cancelled by destroy(), so disabling a keep-alive service mid-click cannot throw 'Object has been destroyed'.

nodes.label: Hung count() released by a timeout race
nodes.rationale: COUNT_TIMEOUT_MS races the count promise so a never-settling tick cannot wedge the busy guard forever; the existing catch reports stale through the dedup and finally clears busy.
nodes.norm_label: hung count() released by a timeout race

nodes.label: One badgeLabel with a 99+ threshold
nodes.rationale: The rail's local badgeText is deleted so tile, switcher and taskbar overlay share one threshold; the dead isQuitting export goes with it.

nodes.label: Task 4 must land before Task 11
nodes.rationale: The count-timeout path reports through the stale dedup, so the dedup must exist first; the Messenger rewrite is behaviour-preserving with the fixture count of 3 as its guard.

nodes.label: Security hardening plan
nodes.rationale: Hardens against local malware (threat A), hostile service pages (threat B) and a tampered supply chain (threat C); pure decision logic lives in tested helpers and only thin wiring touches Electron objects.

nodes.label: Electron fuses in electron-builder.yml
nodes.rationale: Removes the run-as-node / NODE_OPTIONS / --inspect code-exec paths and encrypts session cookies via the OS keychain instead of plaintext SQLite; enableRunAsNode is not a valid key and would fail the whole config, and resetAdHocDarwinSignature keeps the ad-hoc signature that notifications depend on.

nodes.label: isSafeExternalUrl scheme allowlist
nodes.rationale: Only http/https may be handed to the OS, so file:, smb: and custom schemes from a hostile page's window.open are dropped; malformed input fails closed.

nodes.label: permissionAllowed origin check
nodes.rationale: Grants only notifications and media, and only when the requesting origin equals the service's own, so a page navigated or redirected elsewhere gets nothing; both the request and check handlers use it.

nodes.label: ipcSenderAllowed sender-origin policy
nodes.rationale: Shell-only channels must come from the shell frame and service channels must come from the frame of the service named in the payload; the register() wrapper resolves the sender's webContents id to a service and drops spoofed or cross-service messages.

nodes.label: NotificationThrottle per-service floor
nodes.rationale: An 800ms floor per service keeps a hostile page or runaway recipe using the Notification shim from spamming the OS notification centre; services are tracked independently.

nodes.label: ALLOWED_HOSTS navigation containment
nodes.rationale: Each service's view may only navigate to its own domain plus the hosts its login flow bounces through; anything else is prevented and opened in the OS browser. Explicitly gated on live-login verification per service — the one task that must not ship on unit tests alone.

nodes.label: SHA-pinned actions and build provenance
nodes.rationale: Every uses: is pinned to an immutable commit SHA with the tag kept as a comment, and attest-build-provenance signs the installers with id-token and attestations permissions.

nodes.label: Renderer CSP tightening
nodes.rationale: Both privileged pages add object-src none, base-uri self and frame-src none; since they load only first-party assets the tighter policy changes nothing functional.

nodes.label: TikTok chat service plan
nodes.rationale: One vertical slice through the existing add-a-service seams: catalog registration, recipe, nav hosts and icons, with no new IPC, permissions or main-process logic.

nodes.label: TikTok DM recipe
nodes.rationale: count() reads the Messages nav badge (with a title fallback and '99+' parsed as 99), ready() waits for the chat list to mount because a logged-out /messages bounces to a login page that must keep the cover up, and the service lands on /messages rather than the feed.

nodes.label: UNCALIBRATED data-e2e selectors
nodes.rationale: Class names are build-hashed so TikTok's own data-e2e hooks are the only durable surface; they are best-effort until a live login pass, and the dated UNCALIBRATED comment must stay verbatim rather than being silently 'fixed'.

nodes.label: TikTok synthesized notification
nodes.rationale: TikTok web delegates to browser push, which Electron lacks (no FCM), so the banner is synthesized from the first chat-list row carrying an unread badge, using textWithEmoji for nickname and preview.

nodes.label: Registration must land atomically
nodes.rationale: Record<ServiceId, …> types force the catalog entry, recipe registration and nav-policy host list to change together, so the task cannot be split across commits with a red typecheck in between.

nodes.label: TikTok hosts added to ALLOWED_HOSTS
nodes.rationale: Without an entry the record lookup throws and every navigation is denied; OAuth-redirect hosts are deferred to the live login pass.

nodes.label: Rail order and existing-install migration
nodes.rationale: tiktok goes immediately before shopee everywhere (user decision), but the settings migration only appends new ids and never reorders a user's rail, so existing installs get it after shopee and must drag it once.

nodes.label: e2e needs ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE unset
nodes.rationale: VS Code shells export ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, which breaks Electron startup, so the definition of done runs e2e under env -u.

nodes.label: UpdateChecker
nodes.rationale: Main-process poller (first check 10s after launch, then every 24h, 10s request timeout). Every dependency arrives as a plain function so it owns no electron objects and stays unit-testable; one in-flight fetch de-dups concurrent calls; timers are disposed on before-quit and never started when unpackaged.

nodes.label: update-check pure version logic
nodes.rationale: parseLatestRelease/compareVersions/isNewer/releaseUrl with REPO hardcoded. The GitHub payload is treated as attacker-shaped input: an unparsable version compares as 0 and isNewer is false, so a garbled running version can never manufacture a permanent update banner.

nodes.label: UpdateState slice on MainState
nodes.rationale: status/latest/announce ride the existing shell:state broadcast, so no new push channel is needed. setUpdate skips the broadcast on an identical patch, the same report-on-change discipline as setRuntime.

nodes.label: Announce gate (latest vs announce)
nodes.rationale: latest is what exists and drives durable surfaces; announce is the transient 'toast this now' signal, withheld while the window is hidden and flushed on the window's show event. lastNotifiedVersion is persisted so a restart never re-toasts the same version.

nodes.label: UpdateToast
nodes.rationale: Self-expiring 8s toast with no close button; hover/focus banks the remainder. Dismissal is a setTimeout rather than animationend because tokens.css forces animation:none under prefers-reduced-motion, which would strand an animation-driven toast on screen.

nodes.label: shouldToast / TOAST_MS
nodes.rationale: Kept pure so the one-line dedup rule is unit-testable: shell:state is re-broadcast on every unrelated change, so a repeat of the same announce value must not re-toast.

nodes.label: Settings gear update dot
nodes.rationale: The durable surface the transient toast leaves behind; clicking it sets focusSection='updates' so Settings scrolls to the Updates section instead of wherever the modal was left.

nodes.label: Automatic checks fail silently
nodes.rationale: Being offline is not news: only check('manual') may set status 'error'. A later failed automatic check must not clobber an already-known available update.

nodes.label: Release URL built from a validated version
nodes.rationale: html_url in the GitHub response is attacker-influenced if the API or DNS is compromised, so the URL is rebuilt in main from a regex-validated version and only opened behind isSafeExternalUrl. The renderer never supplies a URL; the worst a bad payload can do is show a wrong number.
nodes.norm_label: release url built from a validated version

nodes.label: The update fetch lives in main
nodes.rationale: The shell renderer's CSP is default-src 'self', so a renderer-side fetch to api.github.com would be blocked — and the CSP must not be widened.
nodes.norm_label: the update fetch lives in main

nodes.label: Capture matrix (SHOTS)
nodes.rationale: Pure data in scripts/lib/shots.mjs: one entry per committed PNG, cross-product of surfaces and themes, with settingsFor() producing the throwaway profile's settings.json. A unit test locks ALL_SERVICE_IDS to the app catalog so the matrix cannot drift; a hand-written .d.mts is required because tsconfig excludes scripts/ and strict mode rejects an untyped .mjs.

nodes.label: capture-media.mjs capture driver
nodes.rationale: Playwright-Electron launches the real app once per shot against a fresh mkdtemp profile. Deliberately not a tests/e2e spec: CI runs that directory and CI must not repaint committed assets. Reduced motion is emulated so even the animated surfaces are byte-stable.

nodes.label: Screenshots show Goetia's own chrome only
nodes.rationale: A throwaway profile per shot means no account is ever signed in, and only the shell renderer and loading overlay are captured — service views are separate webContents, so a third-party page cannot leak into a committed image. A shot with chat content is a spec violation, not a cosmetic problem.
nodes.norm_label: screenshots show goetia's own chrome only

nodes.label: docs/media/banner.svg
nodes.rationale: One 1200x300 file serves both themes via an internal <style> block with prefers-color-scheme, with CSS custom properties giving a light default for renderers that ignore it. Colours are lifted from resources/icon.svg and tokens.css rather than re-picked; provable headlessly with the existing @resvg/resvg-js devDependency.

nodes.label: MD033 inline-HTML allowlist
nodes.rationale: A showcase README needs a centred banner, theme-aware <picture> screenshots and a folded troubleshooting <details>; the allowlist is deliberately narrow so lint still catches anything wider.

nodes.label: docs/DEVELOPING.md split
nodes.rationale: Developer build/packaging/release notes move out of the README so the README can be a showcase, while the user-facing install wording stays byte-identical because CLAUDE.md requires it to remain in sync with .github/release-body.md.

nodes.label: Badge shot seeds neverHibernate false
nodes.rationale: DEFAULT_SETTINGS.neverHibernate is true for every service, so an enabled service loads a hidden view at startup and its runner reported {0,0} for the logged-out page within ~500ms, overwriting the --goetia-e2e injected count before the screenshot. Seeding neverHibernate:false means no view and no runner, so the injected badge persists. Do not 'fix' this with waits.

nodes.label: resolveActivation
nodes.rationale: Pure rule for which service to activate after the disabled set changes; null means activate nothing. Replaces two fallbacks that activated order[0] even when it was disabled — disabled must mean no tile, no view, no network.

nodes.label: buildDisabledPatch
nodes.rationale: Always emits a full disabled record covering every id in order, because conf persists whole top-level objects and a partial record would not be safe.

nodes.label: Portal (shared ember-portal component)
nodes.rationale: The loading screen's portal animation is lifted into portal.css plus a React component so the welcome hero can reuse it. loading.html keeps its own inline critical-CSS copy because it must paint before any JS arrives — the two copies must be kept in sync, which a unit test guards.

nodes.label: Welcome component
nodes.rationale: Single-screen walkthrough plus service picker plus confirm, sending only the existing settings:update channel so no new IPC surface is added.

nodes.label: Fresh installs start all-disabled
nodes.rationale: DEFAULT_SETTINGS.disabled flips to all true so a fresh profile opens on the welcome screen and no service touches the network until the user picks. Existing e2e specs seed the old defaults explicitly rather than the defaults being kept for their benefit.

nodes.label: Welcome visibility is derived, not a flag
nodes.rationale: The renderer computes 'every service disabled' from existing ShellState — no first-run flag to persist, migrate or get out of sync, and disabling everything in Settings is the supported way back.
nodes.norm_label: welcome visibility is derived, not a flag

nodes.label: Home Screen and Service Composition Plan
nodes.norm_label: home screen and service composition plan

nodes.label: anyOverlayOpen predicate
nodes.rationale: One pure predicate over settingsOpen/switcherOpen/homeOpen. A visible WebContentsView is layered above the renderer, so activating one while a shell surface is up buries it and steals the keyboard.

nodes.label: homeOpen shell surface
nodes.rationale: Session-only boolean on MainState broadcast in ShellState, never persisted to settings.json; the renderer derives showWelcome = homeOpen || allDisabled. Opening it focuses the shell webContents so Escape and accelerators reach the shell rather than the buried view.

nodes.label: activate(id, { show: false }) — resolve without revealing
nodes.rationale: Splits activation resolution from view presentation: the view is created and z-ordered but stays hidden and unfocused, and showActive() presents it when the surface closes. This is the fix for the settings-modal bug where toggling a service buried the modal it was toggled from.
nodes.norm_label: activate(id, { show: false }) — resolve without revealing

nodes.label: summonDelta / summonLabel
nodes.rationale: The confirm button names the change it is about to apply ('Summon 2 services', 'Banish 1 service', 'Summon 2 · Banish 1', 'No changes'), because banishing tears down a logged-in view and deserves its own word. Returns disabled:true exactly when the delta is empty, which later becomes Dispel's disabled state too.

nodes.label: Rail home sigil and the ⌘/Ctrl 0 accelerator
nodes.rationale: A leading rail button rendering the Portal plus a plain Go>Home menu item with CmdOrCtrl+0 — a plain item rather than a checkbox because buildAppMenu only rebuilds on order and disabled changes, so a checkmark would go stale. Never globalShortcut.
nodes.norm_label: rail home sigil and the ⌘/ctrl 0 accelerator

nodes.label: Composition lives on Home, not Settings
nodes.rationale: An enable toggle behind a modal is what let a service view bury the modal it was toggled from, so the Settings Services pane keeps only mute/never-hibernate/reload for already-enabled services and offers 'Manage services…' which closes Settings and opens Home in one step.
nodes.norm_label: composition lives on home, not settings

nodes.label: resolveStartupSurface
nodes.rationale: The whole launch decision as one pure function: a recorded service that is still enabled wins; no record at all keeps the old rail-order behaviour (a fresh install or an upgrade from a build predating the field is not a failed restore); anything unrestorable resolves a service underneath and opens Home.

nodes.label: rememberSurface / setHomeOpen
nodes.rationale: Every writer of activeId/homeOpen routes through these two, including the ⌘/Ctrl 0 menu path that previously mutated ctx.state.homeOpen directly. setHomeOpen deliberately does not move focus — the accelerator and the IPC handler differ there, and unifying them is out of scope.

nodes.label: Settings.lastActiveId + lastHomeOpen
nodes.rationale: normalize() deliberately does not scrub an unknown lastActiveId: 'recorded but gone' must read differently from 'never recorded', and only the raw value carries that difference. Settings and the quick switcher are modals you pass through, so only Home is recorded as a destination.

nodes.label: Record the surface on change, not at quit
nodes.rationale: Force-quit, a crash and an OS restart never run before-quit, so the record is written the moment the surface changes instead of on the way out.
nodes.norm_label: record the surface on change, not at quit

nodes.label: An unrestorable record opens Home
nodes.rationale: A recorded service that is now disabled or gone from the catalog cannot be honoured, so the launch hands the choice back through Home rather than silently substituting a different service — and Home is activated with show:false so Escape reveals a live service underneath.

nodes.label: Welcome Sections, Dispel and Selling Points Plan
nodes.norm_label: welcome sections, dispel and selling points plan

nodes.label: welcomeSections partition
nodes.rationale: Splits the picker into SUMMONED and UNBOUND in rail order, keyed on the live enabled set so the sections re-sort only when a confirm lands.

nodes.label: Sections follow the live enabled set, tiles follow the staged one
nodes.rationale: The one bug this feature can have: deriving sections from `selected` still compiles and looks plausible, but tiles teleport between sections as you click them. Two independent axes — membership from settings.disabled, glow from the staged selection — is what keeps a deselected tile in place under the cursor.
nodes.norm_label: sections follow the live enabled set, tiles follow the staged one

nodes.label: Dispel button
nodes.rationale: Abandons a staged edit in place by reusing the reseed the screen already performs on every visit, and reuses summonLabel().disabled for its own disabled state so no second predicate enters the codebase.

nodes.label: Three non-overlapping selling-point cards
nodes.rationale: 'Chat only', 'Stays signed in', 'Quiet & light' replace overlapping keyboard-shortcut tips; the hint line below the sections becomes the single place ⌘/Ctrl 0 is taught, with Settings>Shortcuts still listing every binding. No test asserts the copy — a Playwright assertion would only restate the source.

nodes.label: Home Board and Service Ordering Plan
nodes.norm_label: home board and service ordering plan

nodes.label: Catalog sorted by display name
nodes.rationale: SERVICES and DEFAULT_SETTINGS.order both ship in display-name order so the shipped default is predictable, locked by an invariant test. Re-sorting broke 10 fixture tests in 5 files and no behaviour — every expectation was recomputed rather than derived by hand.

nodes.label: moveTo drag index arithmetic
nodes.rationale: Extracted from Rail.tsx before Home could share it, with the shipped splice semantics pinned by test (`to` resolves before the removal, so a forward move lands one slot short). The unknown-id guard is the one addition: with two callers a -1 index would splice from the end.

nodes.label: byName
nodes.rationale: Catalog ids in display-name order: the Unbound order, and the arrival order when several services are summoned at once, since a Set carries no click order.

nodes.label: matchesQuery substring filter
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not the quick switcher's fuzzyScore: that ranks candidates for a jump-to where a stray match costs one glance, while this filters a grid the user is looking at, where 'tg' surfacing Instagram beside Telegram reads as a bug.

nodes.label: summonOrder append-on-summon
nodes.rationale: Newly summoned ids move to the end of the rail so an arrival lands where the user last looked; a banished id keeps its slot and appends like any other arrival if it returns. Sent in the same settings:update patch as `disabled`, never as a second message, so no frame broadcasts an order and enablement that disagree.

nodes.label: ServiceBand
nodes.rationale: Band chrome plus its own overflow-y scroll container, so tile growth stops at the band and never reaches the page. The label row's `aside` slot carries the search box at no vertical cost, and the count stays the unfiltered total.

nodes.label: Home board layout
nodes.rationale: Fixed header / flexible bands / pinned footer with min-h-0 throughout, so the bands shrink instead of the page growing: at the 600px window minimum the bands scroll internally and the Dispel/Summon row stays visible. Summoned is capped at 46% so a long list cannot crowd Unbound out.

nodes.label: WelcomeIntro (first run only)
nodes.rationale: Portal, title, tagline and the three tip cards are onboarding: they earn their space once, and reclaiming it is what gives the steady-state board room to spare. The steady state shows a 14px header instead.

nodes.label: PickTile
nodes.rationale: Moved out of Welcome.tsx with the same molten-squircle language as the rail's active tile. Its `on` prop means 'is staged on' and is the only thing driving the face, so a SUMMONED tile with on=false already renders the staged-to-banish look — no extra ring or badge. The name truncates because a two-line label would push its whole row taller.

nodes.label: Unbound search and the Escape ladder
nodes.rationale: The query is read through a ref so the window listener registers once and never closes over a stale value; the first Escape clears the query, the second leaves Home. No autoFocus — Home is a place, not a modal, and stealing the keyboard would break ⌘/Ctrl 0 muscle memory and take arrow keys from the tiles.
nodes.norm_label: unbound search and the escape ladder

nodes.label: Slack service catalog entry
nodes.rationale: Goetia's ninth service: id slack, url https://app.slack.com/client, colour #4A154B, waitForReady true, slotted between shopee and telegram to keep name order. /client lands on the last-active workspace and Slack's own switcher rail covers the rest, so multi-workspace handling is out of scope.

nodes.label: slack recipe
nodes.rationale: Discord-shaped: the whole client under app.slack.com/client is chat, so there is no chatPaths containment and the css block is purely cosmetic. count() sums numeric mention badges into direct (title '(n)' fallback) and counts badge-less unread, non-muted channels as indirect, scoped to the sidebar so the ~2s poll stays cheap. No synthNotification — Slack fires its own in-page HTML5 notifications.

nodes.label: tests/fixtures/slack.html count oracle
nodes.rationale: The fixture is the oracle for the unread count (2+1 badges -> direct 3, two badge-less unread channels -> indirect 2, one muted and one read channel counting nothing), and blank.html proves count() returns zeros and never throws.

nodes.label: ALLOWED_HOSTS slack entry
nodes.rationale: app.slack.com/slack.com/www.slack.com only: per-user workspace hosts ({team}.slack.com) and the Google/Apple SSO bounce hosts cannot be listed statically, so suffix matching plus a live login pass are prerequisites before the navigation guard can be wired for slack.

nodes.label: Slack logo and notification icons
nodes.rationale: A simple-icons glyph with fill=#ffffff added, nested whole by the icon build script onto the aubergine tile; the notification-icons test iterates SERVICES, so forgetting to regenerate fails the suite instead of shipping a blank slot.

nodes.label: Selectors uncalibrated until a live login pass
nodes.rationale: Following the tiktok/instagram precedent, the recipe says so in a comment rather than silently trusting BEM classes and data-qa hooks; the locale-sensitive aria-label rules in the css block are accepted as a no-op in other locales because they are cosmetic.
nodes.norm_label: selectors uncalibrated until a live login pass

nodes.label: Tasks 1–3 are one atomic change
nodes.rationale: The Record<ServiceId, …> types and the waitForReady/SERVICES iteration tests couple the tasks, so intermediate states neither typecheck nor pass the suite — the plan is deliberately red by design until the icons land and has a single commit checkpoint.

nodes.label: applySubsetOrder
nodes.rationale: Reorder.Group only knows the tiles a surface renders, so the reordered visible ids are merged back into the catalog order that also carries disabled ones, pinning every non-member to its index. The `known` filter is load-bearing: an id absent from `full` would still advance the cursor and overwrite a real service's slot.

nodes.label: useTileReorder
nodes.rationale: Reorder.Group is controlled and fires onReorder on every crossing, so the drag runs on a renderer-local draft and reaches main once on onDragEnd — wired straight to IPC one drag would cost a settings write, a full broadcast and an app-menu rebuild per crossing. The draft clears when the broadcast lands, not on commit, so the drop never snaps back for a frame.

nodes.label: enabledKey
nodes.rationale: A deliberately order-insensitive key over enabled membership. Joining ids in settings.order made a drag-reorder change the key without changing the enabled set, so dropping a tile on Home discarded staged Summon picks and cleared the search box; sorted, a reorder is invisible and a summon or dispel still trips it.

nodes.label: Reorder.Item wrapper div
nodes.rationale: Deviation from the spec's Decision 5: wrapping each tile in a Reorder.Item div removes the Motion/Tailwind fight over `transform` at the source — Motion owns the wrapper, Tailwind keeps owning the button — so ServiceTile's scale-105 and PickTile need no change. whileDrag uses drop-shadow rather than boxShadow because the wrapper is a rectangle around a squircle.

nodes.label: consumeDrag
nodes.rationale: Pointer drag does not suppress the trailing click the way HTML5 DnD did, so an unswallowed one would activate or toggle the tile just dragged. onPointerDown resets the flag, otherwise a drag ending off the tile would leave it set and swallow the next genuine click.

nodes.label: layoutScroll on the band scroll container
nodes.rationale: Without it, a drag inside a scrolled Summoned band computes crossings against stale rects; layoutScroll is what lets Motion correct for the scroll offset.
nodes.norm_label: layoutscroll on the band scroll container

nodes.label: motion as a devDependency
nodes.rationale: electron-vite bundles the renderer, so motion belongs beside react in devDependencies and must never appear in the packaged node_modules — anything in dependencies ships inside the asar. Motion writes transforms through CSSOM, which the default-src 'self' CSP permits.

nodes.label: Goetia Chat Client Design Spec
nodes.author: quyennv + Claude
nodes.rationale: The founding spec: a local-only personal desktop aggregator for five services with native notifications and unread badges — Ferdium's core feature set without its server, accounts or 100-service marketplace. Priorities: fast, stable, clean modern design.

nodes.label: Webview wrapper service integration
nodes.author: quyennv + Claude
nodes.rationale: Each service is its own official web app in a WebContentsView. Native protocol clients were rejected because only Telegram has an official personal API, the reverse-engineered WhatsApp/Messenger/Discord libraries violate ToS and risk account bans, and Zalo has nothing; a TDLib hybrid adds complexity for marginal gain.

nodes.label: Electron as the desktop shell
nodes.author: quyennv + Claude
nodes.rationale: Bundled Chromium means identical rendering on mac and Windows. Tauri v2 was rejected because it means testing two webview engines (WKWebView/WebView2), has weaker multi-webview session isolation, and some chat web apps degrade on non-Chrome engines; CEF is too much plumbing.

nodes.label: Per-service persist: session isolation
nodes.author: quyennv + Claude
nodes.rationale: Every service gets its own persistent partition so cookies, logins and storage never bleed across services — the property that lets several accounts coexist with no server or account system.

nodes.label: Per-service unread recipes
nodes.author: quyennv + Claude
nodes.rationale: A small per-service script adapted from ferdium-recipes (Apache-2.0) extracts {direct, indirect} counts from the page on an interval, with document-title parsing as the fallback. Recipes ship in-repo — no marketplace, no user-installable recipes.

nodes.label: Badge aggregator
nodes.author: quyennv + Claude
nodes.rationale: Folds per-service counts into rail badges, the macOS dock count, the Windows taskbar overlay and the tray tooltip — one fold, four surfaces.

nodes.label: Notification router
nodes.author: quyennv + Claude
nodes.rationale: Receives notifications intercepted by the preloads, shows a native Notification carrying the service name/icon, and on click focuses the app and activates the source service. Honours per-service and global mute.

nodes.label: Hibernation controller
nodes.author: quyennv + Claude
nodes.rationale: Destroys background webContents after an idle timeout (default 30 min) and recreates on activation, bounding RAM growth across many web apps. A hibernated service cannot count unread or notify, hence the per-service never-hibernate override for the ones that must stay live.

nodes.label: Graphite minimal design system
nodes.author: quyennv + Claude
nodes.rationale: Dark-first neutral surfaces, one accent, hairline borders over shadows, a slim icon rail with 44px tiles at radius 10, tabular badge numerals. Chosen so the shell stays quiet beside the embedded services' own UIs; native vibrancy/Mica is finicky in Electron and an expressive palette would clash.

nodes.label: Unisolated per-service preload
nodes.author: quyennv + Claude
nodes.rationale: The per-service preload runs in the page context (contextIsolation:false, sandbox:false, nodeIntegration:false) because a context-isolated preload cannot wrap window.Notification. The shell renderer keeps full context isolation.

nodes.label: Stale-count dot instead of a wrong number
nodes.author: quyennv + Claude
nodes.rationale: When a service ships a redesign the recipe falls back to title parsing, and if that fails too the tile shows a neutral 'count may be stale' dot rather than a confident zero. Fixture-backed parser tests make a redesign a red test instead of a silent wrong badge.
nodes.norm_label: stale-count dot instead of a wrong number

nodes.label: Viber excluded
nodes.author: quyennv + Claude
nodes.rationale: Viber has no web client at all — its desktop app is a native QR-paired client with nothing embeddable — and correspondingly no ferdium recipe exists, so it is an explicit non-goal rather than a backlog item.

nodes.label: Chrome user-agent override
nodes.author: quyennv + Claude
nodes.rationale: Per-session UA with the Electron/x.y token stripped. Required, not cosmetic: WhatsApp Web and Google-family login flows block unknown user agents.

nodes.label: App-level toasts
nodes.author: quyennv + Claude
nodes.rationale: Bottom-right, on bg-2, ~4s, reserved for app-level events such as a crashed service or an available update — never per-message noise, which the OS notification path owns.

nodes.label: Tag-push matrix build to GitHub Release
nodes.rationale: A v* tag builds mac (arm64 + x64 dmg) and Windows (nsis) in a fail-fast matrix, then a separate release job attaches the installers explicitly. workflow_dispatch is a dry run that uploads run artifacts and skips the release. Build-only artifacts were rejected because users would have to dig through Actions runs.
nodes.norm_label: tag-push matrix build to github release

nodes.label: Unsigned builds
nodes.rationale: No certificates, so CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY is false to skip mac signing cleanly and the README carries the first-launch escape hatches (macOS Gatekeeper, Windows SmartScreen). Signing and notarization are deliberately deferred until distribution widens — which also rules out auto-update.

nodes.label: electron-builder keeps publish: null
nodes.rationale: Built-in GitHub publishing would need publish: github in electron-builder.yml, leaking publish behaviour into every local build and producing draft releases with less control. Uploading from the workflow keeps local packaging inert.

nodes.label: Tag ↔ package.json version guard
nodes.rationale: A tag-run step fails before packaging if the tag is not 'v' + package.json version, so a mismatched release can never be published; the release job additionally requires both matrix legs to have succeeded.

nodes.label: Notification Service Icons Design
nodes.rationale: Goal: tell one service from another in the OS banner without reading it.

nodes.label: Brand-colour tile notification icon
nodes.rationale: The service's white glyph on its brand-colour tile, passed as a file path to the native Notification.icon (UNNotificationAttachment on darwin, appLogoOverride on win32). A composite app+service image was rejected because the app icon would then appear twice on macOS, and a bare white glyph is invisible on a light-mode banner. Nothing is decoded or retained in main.

nodes.label: build-notification-icons.mjs
nodes.rationale: Reads SERVICES from the TypeScript source directly, so there is no duplicated service table to drift, and rasterises a wrapper SVG with @resvg/resvg-js at build time with the PNGs committed — neither a normal build nor electron-builder needs the rasteriser. Geometry comes from named ratio constants lifted from ServiceTile, and the logo is nested whole rather than having its path extracted.

nodes.label: extraResources over asarUnpack
nodes.rationale: asarUnpack would leave the icons at an app.asar/... path that only Node's patched fs can resolve, so a path handed to native code would miss. extraResources puts them at process.resourcesPath — a real file everything can open — and the files list excludes them so they are not packed twice.

nodes.label: notificationTitle fallback
nodes.rationale: Dropping the '— <Service>' title suffix removes the guarantee that a title is never blank, so a pure builder falls back to the service name and a recipe emitting an empty sender can no longer produce a headless banner.

nodes.label: 28 px tile inside the 38 pt macOS slot
nodes.rationale: Two variants per service: the plain PNG fills the canvas for Windows, where the tile *is* the app-icon slot and padding would read as broken, while the -mac variant bakes transparent padding in — the only dimension of the attachment box the app actually controls.
nodes.norm_label: 28 px tile inside the 38 pt macos slot

nodes.label: Every service has both PNG variants
nodes.rationale: The test that earns its keep: iterating SERVICES on disk means adding a service without re-running the icon build fails the suite instead of shipping a blank notification slot.
nodes.norm_label: every service has both png variants

nodes.label: We do not own the banner layout
nodes.rationale: macOS fixes the app icon, timestamp and attachment positions with no API to add, move or resize a second icon, so the only lever is how much of the attachment box the artwork fills. A custom frameless banner window would win layout control but forfeit Do Not Disturb, Notification Center history, OS grouping and multi-display placement.
nodes.norm_label: we do not own the banner layout

nodes.label: Service Loading Screen Design
nodes.rationale: Activating a service showed the raw page mid-load — Messenger's Facebook header before the recipe CSS lands, Shopee's shopping homepage for seconds before the mini-chat expands. Every load (cold start, hibernation wake, manual reload, crash auto-reload) is hidden behind a branded screen.

nodes.label: ServiceRuntime.waking state machine
nodes.rationale: 'The loading screen should cover this service.' Set true on view creation and did-start-loading (SPA-internal navigation does not fire it, so no spurious overlay mid-use); cleared by the first of service:ready, did-finish-load for services without waitForReady, the 10s timeout, a crash or the view being destroyed — the last one so a hibernated tile does not breathe forever. The transitions live in a pure, unit-testable module.

nodes.label: Recipe ready(doc)
nodes.rationale: did-finish-load fires long before chat is usable on an SPA, so readiness is per-recipe: messenger waits for chat-list rows, shopee for the mini-chat's expanded header+body. The preload polls every 250ms after DOMContentLoaded and sends service:ready once; a throwing ready() counts as not-ready and the timeout still resolves it.

nodes.label: ServiceMeta.waitForReady consistency
nodes.rationale: Tells main that did-finish-load must not clear waking for that service. A unit test asserts the flag matches which recipes actually define ready(), so the two cannot drift.

nodes.label: 10 s timeout reveal
nodes.rationale: Login walls, captchas and Shopee's anti-bot page can never signal ready, so after 10s the page is revealed as-is with no extra UI. Worst case for a drifted ready selector is the old behaviour delayed — never a lockout behind a spinner.

nodes.label: Overlay above a still-visible view
nodes.rationale: Hiding the service view would break Shopee, whose readiness depends on a synthetic trusted click that cannot reach an invisible view (the existing workaround flashes it visible, and a 300ms reveal flash would defeat the feature). An in-page veil was also rejected: it lives in hostile third-party DOM and must survive redirects. Keyboard focus staying with the covered view is accepted, unchanged behaviour.

nodes.label: Ember Portal animation
nodes.rationale: The app icon decomposes naturally into a spinning fire ring (~2s/turn) and a breathing core (~2.4s) as inline SVG over --bg-0, with rail tiles breathing while their service wakes. No React on the loading page — one static SVG, CSS animations and a single IPC listener updating the caption and data-theme, so it paints before any framework arrives, and the global prefers-reduced-motion rule disables it all.

nodes.label: Shopee Chat Focus Design
nodes.rationale: Shopee shipped as a plain embed of /webchat, which tripped the anti-bot wall on every launch and showed the shopping homepage instead of chat. Reworked so the buyer mini-chat fills the view like every other service.

nodes.label: Homepage entry URL, never /webchat
nodes.rationale: /webchat serves verify/captcha?...scene=crawler_item on every launch and repeated hits risk flagging the account, so the supported entry is shopee.vn/ and the expanded-state CSS also hides the panel header whose expand button navigates back into /webchat. Reload robustness needs no code: the css is re-injected on every DOMContentLoaded and reload lands on the homepage.

nodes.label: Recipe CSS gated on the expanded state
nodes.rationale: Every rule hangs off :has() on the panel's body child, using stable ids only (#main, #shopee-mini-chat-embedded) because every class below them is build-hashed. Live testing showed ungated rules stretch the collapsed pill into a blank white view and would invisibly hide a captcha, so while collapsed the page stays completely untouched and the pill keeps its real rect for keepAlive.
nodes.norm_label: recipe css gated on the expanded state

nodes.label: keepAlive trusted click on the collapsed pill
nodes.rationale: Returns the collapsed pill's centre — the pill element itself, not the host, which may be restyled — reusing the Zalo trusted-click machinery at one click per 30s, and returns null once expanded. It is the only synthetic input the design permits, deliberately, on a platform that already served a captcha.
nodes.norm_label: keepalive trusted click on the collapsed pill

nodes.label: Unread from host textContent
nodes.rationale: Shopee titles never carry '(n)', so the count is the first integer in the host's header or pill textContent, falling back to 0 when the badge is absent — display:none keeps textContent readable, which is why the chrome is hidden rather than removed.

nodes.label: No network filtering
nodes.rationale: webRequest blocking makes the client look more bot-like to a platform that already served a captcha and risks breaking login; the hidden shopping shell loads once and idles, which is cheaper than the risk.

nodes.label: Hardening & remediation design
nodes.rationale: Records every accepted finding from two code reviews plus a defensive security audit, with a fix-or-accept decision each, so the work can execute as two focused plans.

nodes.label: Owner threat model (A local malware, B hostile web content, C supply chain)
nodes.rationale: Scoping the security half to three named threats is what lets findings be triaged as fix-vs-accept instead of chased indefinitely: A steals the six persist: session cookies or abuses the signed binary, B is an XSSed/MITMed service view escaping or navigating away, C is a tampered app/update chain reachable locally.
nodes.norm_label: owner threat model (a local malware, b hostile web content, c supply chain)

nodes.label: Electron fuses block
nodes.rationale: Critical finding: insecure defaults ship, so the binary is usable as a Node interpreter/debug target, cookies are plaintext SQLite, and asar is unvalidated. Disabling runAsNode/node-options/cli-inspect and enabling cookie encryption + asar integrity + load-only-from-asar is the single highest-payoff change for threat A.

nodes.label: External URL scheme allowlist
nodes.rationale: shell.openExternal handed any scheme (file:, smb:, custom) from a hostile page's window.open straight to the OS; only http:/https: may pass.

nodes.label: Permission handler origin check
nodes.rationale: The handler granted camera/mic to every service with no origin check; grants must be validated against the service's own origin and narrowed to what a service actually needs.

nodes.label: Navigation containment guard
nodes.rationale: A hostile page can navigate the top-level view — preload riding along — to an attacker origin and persist as a phishing surface. A will-navigate/will-redirect host allowlist fixes it, but the allowlist must carry each service's real auth-redirect hosts, verifiable only by live login, so it is the highest-effort item and sequenced last.

nodes.label: IPC sender/origin validation
nodes.rationale: Page JS cannot currently reach privileged channels (the preload's ipcRenderer is closure-bound, not on window) except the intentional Notification shim — but there is zero defense in depth. Channels get classified shell-only vs service, and service channels must have their serviceId match the sending frame.

nodes.label: Per-service notification rate limit
nodes.rationale: A hostile page using the Notification shim can spam native banners; the router enforces a per-service minimum interval.

nodes.label: Release supply-chain SHA pinning and provenance
nodes.rationale: Release workflow actions were pinned to mutable major tags with no build provenance — SHA-pin every action and attest the build.
nodes.norm_label: release supply-chain sha pinning and provenance

nodes.label: Renderer CSP tightening
nodes.rationale: object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-src 'none' added to index.html and loading.html as defense in depth — the renderer itself is not attacker-controlled.

nodes.label: Accepted residual risk
nodes.rationale: Same-user malware on an unlocked machine can keylog, screen-capture, and relaunch with --remote-debugging-port regardless of any fix. The fuses close only the silent, no-relaunch paths. Notarization is a distribution-trust measure, not a local-tamper fix, so it is out of scope; asar integrity covers local tampering more cheaply. deleteAppDataOnUninstall stays false so persist: sessions survive reinstalls.

nodes.label: Close-to-tray off must quit
nodes.rationale: With the setting off the window was destroyed but the process lived on, so broadcast() and tray handlers threw on a destroyed window — actually quit, and guard both with isDestroyed().

nodes.label: Crash-reload dwell before counter reset
nodes.rationale: Any successful did-finish-load reset the attempt counter, so a page that loads then repeatedly dies reloads forever; only a minimum uptime dwell may clear the count.

nodes.label: Single-pass Messenger count()
nodes.rationale: Two getComputedStyle calls per read row over overlapping element sets, every 2s forever. One traversal computing style once per element is behaviour-preserving (the fixture still yields 3); deeper selector narrowing needs live DOM.

nodes.label: Bounded startReadyPoll
nodes.rationale: The 250ms poll ran forever on logged-out pages where ready() never turns true; bound it to roughly the wake timeout, since a late reveal cannot re-cover the current load anyway.

nodes.label: Stale-report dedup and no-op setRuntime
nodes.rationale: A persistently failing recipe fired a full ShellState broadcast plus React re-render every tick; report stale only on the transition into stale, and skip the change notification on a genuine no-op patch.

nodes.label: Coalesced window-resize layout
nodes.rationale: Resize re-bounded every view per event; layout() becomes one trailing call per burst.

nodes.label: Per-field settings normalize coercion
nodes.rationale: normalize assumed order is an array, so a corrupt settings.json threw on every hot path and bricked startup; coerce each field with a per-field default fallback.

nodes.label: Runner count() timeout race
nodes.rationale: The busy flag could wedge forever on a hung count(); racing count() against a timeout clears busy and reports stale instead.
